# The reference build — the Sphinx-Needs capture of `examples/basic`

One byte capture, `needs.json`: what `swcraft generate needs --project examples/basic/swcraft.yaml`
writes, which is the `examples/basic/dist/needs.json` of `python scripts/dev.py build`. Two tests
read it, each comparing bytes:

- `test_editing_invariants.py::TestTheExporterProducesTheSameBytesAsBeforeThisPhase::test_the_needs_json_is_byte_identical`
  generates it from `examples/basic/model`;
- `test_cli.py::TestCliGenerate::test_cli_generate_needs_writes_the_file_and_exits_0` runs the CLI on
  a copy of the project.

The earlier captures — `model.c4`, `requirements.rst` and the four files of `needs/` — were deleted
with their generators. The LikeC4 exporter was removed with the diagram generator's arrival
(`f42f4ca3f`, which deleted `model.c4` here); the compositions before-copy
`arxml_golden/differences/before/model.c4` and its entry in `arxml_golden/differences.json`, read by nothing
since, went in the 2026-11-12 clean-up. The dated sections at the end of this file are the
re-captures' records: what moved and what pinned the half that did not. The ARXML half has never been
re-taken.

**Provenance.** The first capture was generated by the code at commit `058e652` — the editing
protocol's base — against the `examples/basic` model, which the editing protocol does not touch. It
is the "before" half of the exporter regression assertion in
`packages/tools/tests/test_editing_invariants.py`.

**Why the ARXML is not here.** The ARXML half is compared against
`../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml` instead, by `test_the_arxml_is_byte_identical` in the same class,
which is a stronger record: that capture was committed with the first-party writer, long before the
editing protocol existed, so "byte-identical before and after" is checked there against a record no
editing work could have influenced.

**The capture serves the editing authorization change too.** It re-generated the captures at its
base commit `5580d05` and confirmed them byte-identical to what was stored here — the editing protocol
changed no generated byte, so its base capture *is* the later base capture. That is why no second
capture and no second digest mechanism was created: a fixture regenerated per change would compare
each change only against its immediate predecessor, while these files hold the whole chain back to
`058e652`, and the ARXML half back to the first-party writer. A later change that re-points this
evidence should do the same — confirm, and record the confirmation here — rather than refresh the
bytes.

**What a failure means.** Both changes classify their Qualification Impact as `None` on the strength
of these comparisons: the editing protocol reads the model through the same reader and snapshot the
generators use, and the claim is that it changed no generated byte. A difference in either
re-classifies the change and must be investigated rather than absorbed by refreshing this file.

## 2026-08-23 — the C4 views change re-took `model.c4`, and why that was legitimate

`model.c4` is **no longer** the `058e652` capture. It was re-generated from
`examples/basic` on 2026-08-23 by the C4 views change, on top of `fca8a2e`, and it
records two deliberate changes to `writer/c4_generation.py`:

- **a populated `views { }` block** — `view index`, `view components`,
  `view tasks` and one `view group_<group>` per non-empty SWC group, where the
  file previously carried the sequence `dynamic view` alone. `index` is emitted
  unconditionally: a document that declares none is one LikeC4 synthesizes an
  all-elements landscape view for, which is the diagram the declarations replace;
- **`variant sequence`** on every `dynamic view`, one line after `title`.

**This is the "investigate rather than refresh" the paragraph above asks for, and
the investigation is a test, not a paragraph.** `packages/tools/tests/test_c4_views.py`
(deleted with the generator) was written *first* (commit `fca8a2e`, four of its cases deliberately
red) and held the half that was not supposed to move: the `specification { }`
and `model { }` blocks come out byte-identical to the pre-change capture, and
every captured `dynamic view` body line still comes out verbatim and in order
with exactly one inserted line. It pinned that against **two** models — this one
and a synthetic layered model with a populated `systems/` layer (and a
`containers/` one until contract `4.0.0` retired that layer), which neither reference
project has. The pre-change bytes of this file were
frozen in that module as the `BASIC_CAPTURE` literal, so the comparison did not
read the file it re-captured.

**The other two comparisons did not move** *in the C4 views change*. `requirements.rst`
was still the `058e652` capture at that point and `test_the_rst_is_byte_identical`
compared against it; the ARXML half is still `../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml`,
the first-party writer's record. The change's Qualification Impact rests on those two being
unmoved and on `.c4` carrying no qualification claim: it is a diagram artifact,
read by no generator and by neither `validate` nor `check-model`.

**What this entry does not cover.** It is a record of *what changed and why it
was allowed*, not a re-derivation of the whole chain: for the `058e652` →
`5580d05` confirmations see the sections above.

## 2026-08-29 — the hardware layer change re-took **both** files, and what stayed identical

The hardware layer change replaced the `resources` layer with a `hardware` layer whose cores and
memories are elements with names, and made `Task.core` a **reference** to a core's
name instead of an integer matched against a budget's `core` field. The reference
model changed with it — `examples/basic/model/resources/{Core0,RAM}.yaml` became
`hardware/{CPU,CORE0,RAM0}.yaml` — so both rendered documents move. Every line of
both diffs was read before the re-capture, and each is one of the renames or the
one removed field:

- **`model.c4`, one line.** `description "period 10 ms, priority 5, core 0"`
  becomes `... core CORE0`. The generator is unchanged; `Task.core` is a name now.
- **`requirements.rst`, three shapes and nothing else.** The two subsection
  headings follow the elements' names (`Core0` → `CORE0`, `RAM` → `RAM0`, each
  with its underline re-length); `:kind: cpu_core` becomes `:kind: core`, the
  contract's own kind id; and the `:core: 0` field is **gone**, because the
  heading above it is now that same string and printing it twice was the one
  wording decision the re-capture took.

**What did not move, and is the reason this re-capture is not a refresh:**

- **The ARXML is byte-identical** to `../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml`, the
  first-party writer's record, and `test_the_arxml_is_byte_identical` still compares against
  it unchanged. That is the whole Qualification Impact claim of the change:
  `layer:hardware` is `arxmlBound: false` and no task, core or memory is emitted.
- **Every figure in the RST is the same number.** `:utilization: 12.00%`,
  `:threshold: 70.00%`, `:headroom: 58.00%`, `:size: 262144 bytes`,
  `:consumption: 3584 bytes`, `:budget: 209715.2 bytes`, `:headroom: 206131.2
  bytes` and the whole per-consumer table are unchanged: the change moved the
  analysis's *input*, not its arithmetic.
- **Every requirement directive** above the Resource Utilization section, and the
  entire `specification { }` and `model { }` structure of the `.c4` beyond the one
  description string.

## 2026-09-06 — the compositions change left `model.c4` deliberately stale (SUPERSEDED by the section below)

Contract `4.0.0` retires the `containers` layer for `compositions`, and the first
step of that change removed the container rendering from `writer/c4_generation.py`
without adding the composition rendering that replaces it. So this file no longer
matched what `swcraft generate c4` produced for `examples/basic`, and the `.c4` byte
comparison of `test_editing_invariants.py::TestTheExporterProducesTheSameBytesAsBeforeThisPhase`
(retired with the generator) was **red on purpose** until the composition rendering re-took it.

Two lines move, and both are removals rather than rewrites:

- `specification { }` loses `  element container`. The block is emitted from a
  fixed list of element kinds and not from the model, which is why this reaches
  `examples/basic` although it has never declared a container;
- `view index` loses the second half of its predicate and its title becomes
  `"Systems"`, because an `include element.kind = container` naming a kind the
  specification no longer declares is an unresolved reference.

**This is the "investigate rather than refresh" the paragraph above asks for,
and, as in the C4 views change, the investigation is a test.**
`packages/tools/tests/test_c4_views.py` held the half that was not supposed to move, and
it held it against the same two models: the two removals were written there as
the explicit substitutions `SPECIFICATION_CONTAINER_KIND_REMOVAL` and
`CONTAINER_ELEMENT_REMOVAL`, so the byte comparison of the `specification { }`
and `model { }` blocks stayed exact and every other byte of both was still pinned.
The pre-change bytes of this file were frozen in that module as the
`BASIC_CAPTURE` literal, so that comparison did not read the file it was waiting
to re-take.

**The other two comparisons did not move.** `requirements.rst` was still the
hardware layer capture and its byte comparison passed against it; the
ARXML half is still `../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml`, the first-party writer's record,
and `test_the_arxml_is_byte_identical` passes against it — `layer:compositions`
is `arxmlBound: true` in the contract, but no composition is emitted yet and
`examples/basic` declares none, so the delta is nil in both directions.

**What the re-take owes this file**, when it comes: a dated section of its own
naming every line of the diff, in the shape the two sections above use.

## 2026-09-07 — the compositions change re-took `model.c4`, and every line of the diff

The composition rendering landed, so this file **is** what `swcraft generate c4`
produced for `examples/basic` again, and the `.c4` byte comparison (retired with the generator)
was green. The re-capture is not a refresh, and this time the investigation is
**two** tests plus a committed expected difference:

- `packages/tools/tests/fixtures/arxml_golden/differences.json` carries a `c4`
  entry, written by hand from the design **before** the generator emitted a
  composition, and `packages/tools/tests/test_c4_views.py` asserted that the observed
  difference between `../arxml_golden/differences/before/model.c4` (this file's
  bytes at the branch point, sha256 `7bed2be3…`) and this file **equals** it.
  The asserted-difference discipline, applied to the one committed `.c4` exactly as it is
  to the three ARXML goldens;
- `TestTheC4EmissionIsAdditive` still held the half that was not supposed to
  move, through four further admitted substitutions
  (`SPECIFICATION_COMPOSITION_KIND_ADDITION`, `COMPOSITION_LEVEL_REWRITE_BASIC`,
  `RELATIONSHIP_REPARENTING_BASIC` and `DYNAMIC_VIEW_REPARENTING_BASIC`), and
  `TestTheFlatViewsSurviveAsProjections` asserted the flat views' node and edge
  **sets** were unchanged under the reparenting rather than leaving that to a
  reader.

Every line of the diff, and each is one of four differences:

- **`specification { }` trades `element container` for `element composition`.**
  The block is a fixed list of kinds, so this reaches a project whatever it
  declares — the same property that made the container rendering's removal visible here.
- **`Root = composition { … }` is added**, carrying the composition's own
  `title` and `description` from `examples/basic/model/compositions/Root.yaml`.
- **Both components are reparented into it and change order**:
  `ExampleSWC` becomes `Root.ExampleSWC`, and they are emitted in the root's
  declared `members` order (ExampleSWC first) rather than the `swc` layer's read
  order (a layer is read by sorted path, so ExampleConsumerSWC came first). The
  two relationship lines and the sequence step follow the ids. Every title and
  every description is the string it was: a member's own `description` is
  deliberately not rendered, because the box describes the TYPE placed there.
- **One view is added, `view compositions`**, the only static view that includes
  the level. Without it the composition would be an element no view draws.

**What did not move.** `requirements.rst` is untouched — still the hardware layer
capture — and the ARXML half is `../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml`, which the change
re-froze against its own committed difference entry and which
`test_the_arxml_is_byte_identical` compares unchanged. `.c4` output carries no
qualification claim: it is a diagram artifact, read by no generator and by
neither `validate` nor `check-model`.

**What no test here reaches**, and where it was answered instead: whether LikeC4
*renders* the reparented document the way the flat views promise. That was
measured once, with `npx likec4@1.59.2 export json` over this file and over its
before-copy — every flat view's node and edge set identical modulo the `Root.`
prefix, with one addition, `view tasks` gaining the `Root` compound because a
view whose nodes do not all share one ancestor draws the ancestors that differ.
The measurement is the compositions change's; the three-level lift was left to a later
measurement.

## 2026-09-16 — the diagram generator change deleted `model.c4`

`swcraft generate c4` and `writer/c4_generation.py` are gone — the diagram generator
(`swcraft generate diagrams`, `writer/diagrams/`) replaced them — so `model.c4` had no
producer and no reader left: its byte comparison was retired with the generator, and the file
was deleted in the same commit. The sections above are the record of what it was.
`requirements.rst` stayed, compared byte for byte until its own generator left, and the ARXML half
is still `../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml`.

What replaced the `.c4` half is not a capture here: the diagram generator's whole output for
`examples/basic` is the golden `../diagrams_golden/basic/`, frozen by
`test_diagram_generation.py` run as a script, and `dev.py build`'s views are held to it by
`test_dev_build.py`. That the ARXML at both versions and this RST did not move when the C4
generator left is asserted for every committed model tree by
`test_diagram_switch_byte_identity.py`, against digests the branch point's generators wrote.

## 2026-10-16 — the trace link move re-took `requirements.rst` (contract `11.0.0`)

The requirements model moved the trace link from the requirement's `links` into the linked
element's own `satisfies`, and retired the requirement's `status`. `examples/basic`'s
`REQ_EXAMPLE_001` lost `links` and `status`, and `ExampleSWC` and `ExampleConsumerSWC` each
declare `satisfies: [REQ_EXAMPLE_001@1]`. Every line of the diff, and each is one of two
differences:

- **`:status: open` is gone.** The requirement has no `status` field any more, so the
  directive renders none.
- **`:links:` is computed and sorted.** It lists the elements that satisfy the requirement
  (`trace.satisfying_elements`), sorted by name — `ExampleConsumerSWC, ExampleSWC` where the
  retired field's own order was `ExampleSWC, ExampleConsumerSWC`. The two names are the same.

**What did not move.** The directive's title, `:id:` and body, and the whole Resource
Utilization section — every figure and both consumer tables — are byte for byte the hardware layer
capture. The ARXML half is still `../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml`, unchanged: no link was
ever emitted to ARXML, and `examples/basic`'s ARXML digests at both versions in
`test_diagram_switch_byte_identity.RECORDED` did not move, measured against the branch point's
generators (`450b01a8`) on the branch point's tree. The same RST digest was re-measured in that
module's `RECORDED` in the same change.

## 2026-10-18 — the Sphinx-Needs change re-took `requirements.rst` (the Resource Utilization section left)

On 2026-10-18 the Resource Utilization section left the RST: a load

**What did not move.** The `REQ_EXAMPLE_001` directive — title, `:id:`, `:links:` and body — is

`test_diagram_switch_byte_identity.RECORDED` did not move. The RST digest of every committed tree

run on the same trees.

## 2026-10-18 — the Sphinx-Needs change replaced `requirements.rst` with the four files of `needs/`

`swcraft generate rst` writes the Sphinx-Needs export, a folder, where it wrote one file: the
manifest's `outputs.rst` names the folder (default `dist/needs`), and a value ending in `.rst` is
refused. The capture followed: `requirements.rst` at this directory's top is deleted, and `needs/`
holds the four files the command wrote for `examples/basic` (run on a copy of the project, through
the CLI), compared file by file and by name set by `test_editing_invariants.py`:

- **`swcraft-needs.toml` and `swcraft_needs.py`** — the Sphinx-Needs configuration in its two forms.
  They do not depend on the model: the type list is the full fixed set.
- **`requirements.rst`** — a `Requirements` title, then `REQ_EXAMPLE_001`'s directive. Against the
  previous capture it lost `:links: ExampleConsumerSWC, ExampleSWC` (the link now stands on the
  satisfying element's own need) and gained `:source: architecture`, the requirement's declared
  source. Its title, `:id:` and body are unchanged; the id needed no translation.
- **`architecture.rst`** — an `Architecture` title, then `SWC-ExampleConsumerSWC` and
  `SWC-ExampleSWC`, each carrying `:satisfies: REQ_EXAMPLE_001` and its description: the two
  elements the retired `:links:` option named, now needs of their own.

**What did not move.** The ARXML half is still `../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml`, unchanged: the
export was never ARXML, and `examples/basic`'s ARXML digests at both versions in
`test_diagram_switch_byte_identity.RECORDED` did not move. The RST column of that module's
`RECORDED` (and of the byte-identity modules that record the same column) now digests one record
of the four files (`conftest.needs_export_bytes`), re-measured for every committed tree in the same
change with the previous generator and the new one run on the same trees.

## 2026-10-18 — a docstring fix re-took `needs/swcraft_needs.py` (its docstring)

The generated file's docstring told a `conf.py` to write `needs_types += TYPES`,
`needs_fields.update(FIELDS)` and `needs_links.update(LINKS)`, which raises `NameError` in a
`conf.py` that set none of those names — the common case the guide's recipe was written for. The
docstring now states the guide's defensive recipe in a sentence and points to the guide's section
*The Sphinx-Needs export* for the lines. The capture was re-generated from the same code; only the
docstring's lines moved, and the four assignments did not.

**What did not move.** `swcraft-needs.toml`, `requirements.rst` and `architecture.rst` are
unchanged, and so is the ARXML half. The RST column of `test_diagram_switch_byte_identity.RECORDED`
(and of the byte-identity modules that record the same column) moved for every committed tree,
re-measured in the same change with the previous and the new docstring on the same trees.

## 2026-10-18 — a second docstring fix re-took `needs/swcraft_needs.py` (its docstring)

A check found that the guide's recipe replaced Sphinx-Needs' default need types
(`req`, `spec`, `impl`, `test`, `need`) with SWCraft's whenever a `conf.py` set no `needs_types`:
assigning that setting replaces the defaults, so a project's `impl` and `test` directives became
unknown. The recipe now starts from the defaults and adds each of SWCraft's types whose directive
the project does not already declare, and the docstring says so in its sentence. The capture was
re-generated from the same code; only the docstring's lines moved, and the four assignments did not.

**What did not move.** `swcraft-needs.toml`, `requirements.rst` and `architecture.rst` are
unchanged, and so is the ARXML half. The RST column of `test_diagram_switch_byte_identity.RECORDED`
(and of the byte-identity modules that record the same column) moved for every committed tree,
re-measured in the same change with the previous and the new docstring on the same trees.

## 2026-10-19 — a configuration fix re-took `needs/swcraft-needs.toml` and `needs/swcraft_needs.py`

A check found that Sphinx-Needs parses a field's `[[...]]` as a dynamic function by
default (7.0.0 to 9.0.0, measured): a `revision` of `[[release]]` dropped the whole need and one of
`[[copy('id')]]` was evaluated. Every field the configuration declares now sets
`parse_dynamic_functions = false`, one key more per field in both forms. The capture was
re-generated from the same code; only those two files moved, by those seven keys each.

**What did not move.** `requirements.rst` and `architecture.rst` are unchanged — `examples/basic`
holds no `[[`, which a title or a description is now refused for — and so is the ARXML half. The RST
column of `test_diagram_switch_byte_identity.RECORDED` (and of the byte-identity modules that record
the same column) moved for every committed tree, re-measured in the same change with the previous
and the new configuration on the same trees.

## 2026-11-06 — `needs.json` replaced the four files of `needs/`

`swcraft generate rst` and its four Sphinx sources are gone: `swcraft generate needs` writes one
Sphinx-Needs `needs.json` (the manifest's `outputs.needs`, default `dist/needs.json`) that the
requirements team loads into its own documentation, with no Sphinx at the architect's side. The
Sphinx sources echoed every incoming requirement and translated ids, the two things the new file
does not do, and a Sphinx build of them was refused by SWCraft's own import, so they were replaced
rather than kept beside it. `needs/` is deleted, and `needs.json` is what the command wrote for
`examples/basic` (run on a copy of the project, through the CLI), compared byte for byte by
`test_editing_invariants.py`'s `test_the_needs_json_is_byte_identical`:

- **`REQ_EXAMPLE_001`**, the model's one architecture requirement, a need of type `arch_req` with its
  title and its description as the content. It declares no safety level, so no `asil` key.
- **`SWC-ExampleConsumerSWC` and `SWC-ExampleSWC`**, each a need of type `arch_element` tagged `swc`,
  carrying `satisfies: [REQ_EXAMPLE_001]` and its description: the two linked elements the retired
  `architecture.rst` held. The links are confirmed (`REQ_EXAMPLE_001@1` at version 1), so neither is
  `satisfies_unconfirmed`.
- **`current_version` is `""`**: the model holds no imported requirement, so no delivery is named.
- **`swcraft_path`** on each of the three (re-captured the same day,
  2026-11-06): the model-root-relative storage name of the file declaring the need —
  `requirements/REQ_EXAMPLE_001.yaml`, `swc/example/ExampleConsumerSWC.yaml`,
  `swc/example/ExampleSWC.yaml`. Nothing else moved.

The configuration in two forms (`swcraft-needs.toml`, `swcraft_needs.py`) has no successor: the
requirements team declares the three need types, the two fields and the four link types in its own
`conf.py`, as the user guide gives them.

**What did not move.** The ARXML half is still `../arxml_golden/basic-4.2.2.arxml`, unchanged: the
export was never ARXML. The byte-identity modules' RST column is no longer read (its generator is
gone, so no branch point's digest can be re-checked); the ARXML columns they hold did not move.
